newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Australia wheat shipments 7.8 m/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Australia wheat shipments 7.8 m/t.

text.p: Australian wheat shipments rose further in the past week to reach almost 7.8 million tonnes so far this year, nearly double the amount at the same time last year, the Australian wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday.

Exports in the week ended February 28 of 356,123 tonnes took the total so far this year to 7.799 million tonnes, up from 4.462 million tonnes at the same time last year, AWB said in its weekly market report. No significant sales occurred during the week, it said. Japan purchased 180,000 tonnes from the U.S., Canada and Australia under regular buying arrangements.

Longer-term, the AWB successfully negotiated the sale of a minimum of 900,000 tonnes of wheat for the coming season, with 700,000 tonnes expected to come from Western Australia. The remainder, in Australian Prime Hard grade, was expected to be shared between New South Wales and Queensland, the AWB said.
The United States confirmed a US$21 million loan to Jordan to fund wheat purchases, the board said.
On Australia's domestic grain market, AWB said rain delays affecting Queensland's sorghum harvest drove grain prices higher again in the past week.
Increasing demand from the Victorian dairy sector combined with the smaller than expected winter wheat harvest had supported the trend and cash prices in Victoria jumped again.

Demand for milling grade wheats eased, with occasional trades. Most millers had covered their needs for the near-term, it said. Demand for Australian Standard White grade had been fuelled by feed grain interest, it said.

Pulse prices rose substantially, especially in field and chick peas. Demand had emerged from international buyers following concern over the Indian chiuck pea crop, it said. The current wheat crop is still estimated at 23 million tonnes.
